children: Elko, Nevada--(Newsfile Corp. - October 29, 2026) - Lithium Corporation (OTCQB: LTUM) ("Lithium Corporation" or the "Company"), a mineral exploration company focused on advancing North American critical mineral resources, reports the completion of its 2026 field programs at the Big Creek rare earth element (REE) property and Yeehaw titanium/REE property; both located in British Columbia, Canada.

Lithium Corporation staked the Big Creek REE prospect following the Company's Fall 2025 exploration program at its Las Pilas property. All Big Creek claims, covering 10,832-acres (4,383-hectares) in the Midway Range north of Greenwood, were fully granted in late August 2026.

Work at Big Creek included prospecting, geological and geochemical fieldwork, and a preliminary radiometric survey. At Yeehaw, fieldwork consisted of geochemical work and a preliminary radiometric survey. Initial observations suggest radiometric surveys will be an effective tool for tracing mineralized zones that subcrop beneath areas of locally extensive glaciofluvial till. These preliminary findings may help guide future exploration and refine the interpretation of mineralized zones beneath surface cover.

Earlier this year, Lithium Corporation optioned the Company's Las Pilas rare earth element (REE) prospect. At the optionee's request, Linda Caron, MSc, P.Eng., prepared an NI 43-101-compliant technical report. The report recommends a two-stage exploration program with an estimated budget of $100,000. Lithium Corporation is reviewing the recommendations and developing plans to incorporate relevant findings into its broader regional REE exploration strategy.

About Lithium Corporation

Nevada-based Lithium Corporation (OTCQB: LTUM) is a mineral exploration company operating as a project generator, identifying and advancing prospective critical mineral assets across North America. The Company's portfolio includes lithium, rare earth elements and other minerals essential to energy storage and electrification, providing exposure to diverse opportunities within the critical minerals sector and supporting the development of secure North American supply chains.

Through strategic partnerships and partner-funded exploration, LTUM seeks to advance projects while limiting the Company's direct capital commitments. Retained royalty interests preserve exposure to potential future production, creating multiple pathways for value generation across the portfolio while supporting a capital-efficient approach to exploration.
